run_token_cap.description:

org_role.description: Absent: none (`ceo` and `cto` at most once per company).

reports_to.description: An agent of the company it reports to.

runner_tags.description: Capabilities a runner must offer, e.g. `macos`.

The allowlist entry: `<tool>` or `<tool>:<command prefix>`. Absent: the escalated call's

Appearance.description: An agent's figure: which version the client draws, in which palette (`listPalettes`).

payload.description: What is asked, by kind (the sprint's issues, the command, the overrun, …).

left.description: Points left at the end of the day.

account_ids.description: The pool accounts its runs may use (E15.1).

anyOf.description: The admin's own company, or a client's (E15.14).

Runs that used tokens, and what they cost. Dollars are the priced runs' only: an unpriced

raise_tokens.description: A `budget_overrun` is approved with this many more tokens for the period.

reply.description: Goes back to the agent that asked, and wakes it.

anyOf.description: Who may deploy to an environment.

Device.description: A device's key, without the key.

last_used_at.description: Marked at most once a minute.

url.description: Empty when it has none; never holding credentials.

key.description: `KEY-E3`: its project's key and its number there, never reused.

epic_id.description: Absent takes it out of its epic.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,

points.description: Story points; absent clears the estimate.

Event.description: One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

EventPayload.description: What happened. New types may be added: a client skips an event it cannot decode.

EventPayloadAudit.description:
An audited change: `action` is dotted (`issue.in_review`, `run.failed`,
`approval.approved`, …) and names the `entity` it happened to.

EventPayloadTranscript.description: A chunk of a run's transcript.

EventPayloadWake.description: A wake queued for an agent.

Fallback.description: One entry of the chain, tried in order after the agent's own harness and model.

anyOf.description:
What an agent's figure shows, first match wins:

| state | when |
|---|---|
| `sleepy` | the agent is paused |
| `rest` | it waits on its hire approval, or is terminated |
| `listening` | it has an open question to the admin, or an approval it asked for is pending |
| `working` | its run is running and has produced output |
| `thinking` | its run is running, no output yet |
| `loading` | its run is queued or claimed by a runner, not yet started |
| `confused` | its last run failed, timed out, lost its runner or stalled |
| `success` | its last run succeeded in the last five minutes |
| `idle` | otherwise |

age_secs.description: Created → done, or → now while open.

done_at.description: Last done, while it is done.

repos.description: The repos it touches, in the project's order.

IssuedDevice.description: A new device and its key: the only time the key is ever shown.

name.description: One line, 1–50 characters, unique in the project.

LastRepair.description:
An automatic repair (E15.8): its action (`rewake`, `escalate`, …, or `escalate_to_admin`
past the issue's repair budget) and when.

LatestEvent.description: The newest event's seq a client would be shown: the catch-up target.

used.description: Used in the window ending now.

Me.description: The calling device and what it may see.

companies.description:
The companies this key may see: every one, or only the acting one when

user.description: The user it acts as: the one admin.

capacity.description: Points it takes on per sprint; absent when not set.

MessageDelivery.description:
Where a message to a run went: to the run (`message_id`; its harness gets it at its next
turn, shown in the transcript as a `user_message` chunk with that id), or, the run not live,
a comment on its issue waking the run's agent (`comment_id`). A message the run ends before

The (harness, model) an agent's tasks of `tier` start on. Its own harness and model are
its standard tier, so only `small` and `large` are set here.

anchor_issue_id.description: The issue to go before or after.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key on the same issue posts (and wakes) once.

assignee_agent_id.description: An agent to hand it to at once, which wakes it.

input_usd_per_mtok.description: Dollars per million tokens, 0 or more (as `citadel-server price set`).

Issue-number prefix, unique in the company: 1–10 capital letters and digits, starting
with a letter (`CIT` for `CIT-12`).

sprint_approval.description: Who approves a sprint commit; absent: the owner.

team_id.description: The team that owns it, one of the company's.

wake_status.description: `pending`, or `coalesced` into the wake already waiting.

Page_Artifact.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

Page_Event.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

Page_Run.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

woke_agent_id.description: The agent the comment woke: the issue's next actor, else its owner.

A harness and model's price, US dollars per million tokens; each set is a new version, and

`true` (the default): to the top of its backlog, its wakes dispatched first; `false`

Profile.description: A project's profile. Every field may be empty.

definition_of_done.description: Rules an issue meets before it is done.

definition_of_done.description: Rules an issue meets before it is done.

Timestamp.description:
RFC 3339 UTC with exactly milliseconds, `2026-10-21T12:00:00.250Z`: one shape, so a

TranscriptChunk.description: One chunk of a run's transcript, as the runner sent it (redacted).

The payload's `type`: `session_started`, `assistant_text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`,

prs.description: Its pull requests, one per repo it touches.

cost_usd_micros.description: Absent when the run is not priced.

Versions.description: What the server is and speaks.

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

when.description:
`now` ("Wake my Mac": pushed to the Mac app at once; the default) or `when_back` ("Run

info.description: The Citadel client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request carries a device key as `Authorization: Bearer` (never in the URL) and the server's own `Host`, and no `Origin`. A client working in one company sends its id as `X-Citadel-Company`: every route then answers 404 for another company's data, and lists that span companies keep to it. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.
